slides.heading: Numbers In Pi
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Dynamic Programming
slides.narration: Let's solve Numbers In Pi, a hard dynamic programming problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Minimum spaces to split the digit string into numbers all from the given list, or -1.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Minimum spaces to split the digit string into numbers all from the given list, or -1. DP over suffixes.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Find the fewest pieces to cover each suffix of the digits with favourite numbers, using memoisation.
slides.narration: Find the fewest pieces to cover each suffix of the digits with favourite numbers, using memoisation.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
slides.narration: Trying every split is exponential. A DP over suffixes, the fewest spaces from index i onward, is quadratic with a hash set of numbers.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. From each start, try every prefix in the set
3. Recurse on the rest with memo
slides.narration: Step by step. First, put numbers in a set. Second, from each start, try every prefix in the set. Third, recurse on the rest with memo. Fourth, spaces equal pieces minus one.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Dp of n is minus one. From the end backward, for each j, if the rest is solvable and pi from i to j is a favourite, take dp j plus one. Return dp zero or minus one.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n cubed plus m. Space is O of n plus m.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: dp[n] = −1 (no space after the last number)
slides.narration: Seed the end with minus one, because there's no space after the last number.
